name: lp_solve
why: A real mixed integer linear programming solver you can run on toy optimisation problems at home.

brief.what_it_is: lp_solve is a command-line mixed integer linear programming solver. It reads an optimisation model from a file or standard input, in its native LP format or MPS format (or others via the XLI plug-in layer), and prints the objective value plus, depending on the -S detail level, the variable values, constraint values, and dual values. The reference page says the command-line program can use essentially all the functionality of the underlying library. The documented example is a small maximisation with two variables and three constraints, solved with lp_solve -S3 model.lp, which reports an objective of 6315.63.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage is only a frameset stub with no framing text. The command-line reference page states its purpose as a command-line application exposing the library's functionality for reading, solving and writing models, so you can solve a model without writing code against the API.
brief.how_it_works: You point it at a model file (or pipe one in on stdin) and pass options that select the input format, pivot rule, scaling, presolve, branch-and-bound rule, MIP gap and output detail. It writes the solution to the console or a file, and can also write the model, basis or parameters back out. The reference page warns that the input format is not the C API: calls such as make_lp are wrong input here.

commands_seen.context: Solve an LP-format model file with default options.
Solve with automatic scaling enabled (the -s option with no mode).
Solve the documented example model and print objective, variables and constraints.
Read a fixed-format MPS model with scaling and redirect the output to a file.
Same as above but print constraints and dual values (-S4).
Print the full list of options for version 5.5.2.14.
Pipe a model written by a user program on standard output straight into lp_solve, with no intermediate file.
Feed the model through input redirection instead of a file argument.

brief.install_notes: The reference page says there is no installation procedure: you only need the single lp_solve binary (lp_solve.exe on Windows), extracted from lp_solve_5.5.2.14_exe.zip or lp_solve_5.5.2.14_exe.tar.gz. On Windows it must be run from cmd.exe or a batch file, not by double-clicking. Running it with no file argument gives a blinking cursor where you type the model, ended with Ctrl Z, which the page calls awkward. No accounts, runtimes or configuration are mentioned. I did not check the Homebrew formula itself.
brief.standout: It is a single self-contained solver binary that also exposes a large set of simplex, presolve, scaling and branch-and-bound knobs from the command line, and it fits naturally into Unix pipelines with a model generator.
brief.status: Unknown. The reference page names version 5.5.2.14 as current, but I saw no release date, commit history or changelog on the pages I fetched, so I cannot say how recently it was updated.
brief.caveats: The homepage is a frameset stub: it links to menu.htm, which returned HTTP 404, so navigation from the homepage is broken. The reference is the only substantive page I read; the LP-format and MPS-format pages it links to were not fetched. Windows use requires the command line. Licence was not seen on the pages I read.
quotes: The lp_solve program is a command line application that can use as good as all functionality of the library.
There is no installation procedure for this application. There is no need for it.
However it is much better to write your model in a disk file with your favourite editor
